PROVENANCE — real coach records from a real build; DO NOT hand-edit.

What these two files are
  A copy, byte for byte, of two records the coach wrote during a real build on
  6 September 2026. The build is build-FEAT-8388 and the task is
  TASK-8388-002, a feature task on the api_test repository, which keeps its
  database schema in Alembic migrations (alembic/env.py, alembic/versions/).

Where they came from (read-only copy, taken 2026-09-06)
  /home/richardwoollcott/forge-state/receipts/build-FEAT-8388-20260906180545/
    .guardkit/autobuild-private/TASK-8388-002/coach_evidence_turn_1.json
    .guardkit/autobuild-private/TASK-8388-002/coach_turn_1.json

Checksums of the copies (sha256), identical to the source files
  15ae16fb64e12723e40745eb0e758c0f8601d8cec268f3597e302714ad13e1e7  coach_evidence_turn_1.json
  8d1d57c6a4695671e4fadcde8dc6a942de4ef7ef20f7c0f1975ac72de6055558  coach_turn_1.json

Why they are kept here
  coach_turn_1.json is what the coach said on this task's only turn: an
  approval. Its only findings are four should_fix honesty notes about files
  the Player listed but had not touched. Nothing in it mentions the database.

  coach_evidence_turn_1.json is the record of what was checked for that
  verdict. The independent test run passed (50 tests), and the behavioural
  oracle says it ran and passed — but that oracle was testing a Docker image
  built on 25 July, not this build's code.

What the build had actually done (from the build's own log,
autobuild-stdout.log in the receipts directory above, and the Player reports
under its worktrees/FEAT-8388/.guardkit/autobuild/ copy)
  The "domain" column was not added on this task. TASK-8388-002's one turn
  changed nothing: its Player report lists no files, and the log says
  "turn 1 changed 0 file(s) in the worktree (git-measured)" (line 713). The
  four honesty notes are about that.

  The column came in two tasks earlier, on TASK-8388-001 turn 1. The Player
  changed src/users/models.py (the "domain" column) and src/users/schemas.py
  and created tests/users/test_user_domain.py — three files (log line 210) —
  with no Alembic migration. The coach sent that turn back for an unrelated
  reason: the independent test run could not collect any tests (the
  worktree's conftest failed to import), which the coach reads as absent
  evidence, not a pass. The build checkpoints every completed turn, so that
  feedback turn was committed anyway, as fcb67c59 (log lines 247-249), and
  from then on the unmigrated model change was in HEAD. On TASK-8388-001
  turn 2 the Player changed nothing (log line 342) and the coach approved,
  with three advisory notes that the files the Player listed showed no
  change — they had been committed by the turn-1 checkpoint. TASK-8388-002
  then approved as described above, and the build went through.

  The unit tests could not see the gap at any point: they build the schema
  from the model.

  The deploy into the Docker Sandbox then found it: on a freshly created
  database, built by running the migrations, the users table had no "domain"
  column. 44 checks passed and 6 failed, and the candidate was refused.

  A note on the choice of records. The lane's spec (ai-transition,
  docs/rewrite-on-refusal-spec-2026-09-06.md, the provenance-fixture rule)
  names this task's two records and says of them that the model file gained
  "domain". The receipts say the column was added and committed under
  TASK-8388-001. The records kept here are the ones the spec names; this
  note records the difference rather than swapping in other records without
  the spec author's word. TASK-8388-001's turn-1 feedback and turn-2 approval
  are the records that actually carried the unmigrated model through.

How the tests use them
  coach_turn_1.json is a real approval from the build that got through: the
  verdict shape the deterministic check
  AgentInvoker._apply_schema_change_without_migration_guard flips.
  coach_evidence_turn_1.json is the real evidence bundle threaded through the
  real invoke_coach path. The worktree shape the guard reads — an uncommitted
  change to src/users/models.py adding a column, nothing added under
  alembic/versions/ — is built by the tests themselves, because on the real
  build the change was already in a committed checkpoint by the time either
  approval was given.

  The guard reads the worktree's difference from HEAD, which is how the
  lane's spec defines "this turn's changes". Because every completed turn is
  checkpointed, on this build's actual path the guard would have seen the
  three uncommitted files on TASK-8388-001 turn 1 (a verdict already sent
  back, which the guard leaves alone: it only overrides an approval) and
  nothing on the two approved turns, whose trees were clean. Whether it
  should read further back than HEAD is a decision for the spec's author; it
  is recorded in the guard's docstring, not taken here.

No secrets: both files were scanned for API keys and message-broker URLs
before they were copied (zero matches).
